title: git-auto-commit (PostToolUse:Write|Edit) does `git add -A` over ALL of ~/.claude including dist files the background forward-sync is concurrently overwriting -> can snapshot a half-synced active dist into a safety commit
observe_how: git-auto-commit only acts when the edited file is under ~/.claude (isInClaudeDir) -- so it is NOT in the repo-edit path -- but when a DIRECT ~/.claude edit triggers it, doCommit runs `git add -A` (stages everything in ~/.claude). If a forward-sync from a concurrent repo commit is mid-flight, the -A stages a partially-copied dist tree. Debounced to 10min so the window is narrow, but the `add -A` blast radius is wider than the file that triggered it. Payoff: scoping the add to the triggering path (or the debounce key) avoids snapshotting unrelated in-flight sync state.
telemetry: Replace `git add -A` with staging only tracked changes relevant to the edit, or guard with the same sync lock (D10b-02).

title: memory-awareness attaches per-turn memory scores to the PREVIOUS turn's Braintrust span: resolveBraintrustSpan prefers a current_turn_span_id that is one turn stale at UserPromptSubmit time, while the adjacent comment claims root-span attachment and metadata says attached_to:'turn'

evidence.quote:
if (state.current_turn_span_id && state.current_turn_span_id.length > 0) {
    return { spanId: state.current_turn_span_id, attachedTo: 'turn' };

set_session_value(session_id, "turn_count", turn_count)
    set_session_value(session_id, "current_turn_span_id", turn_span_id)

observe_how: The comment is internally inconsistent with the code three lines below it: the code PREFERS current_turn_span_id, falling back to root only when it is empty. Because the Python handler runs after memory-awareness in the UPS chain (settings.json:166 vs :196) and the turn span is never cleared mid-session (D10a-01), the state file at emit time always holds turn N-1's span from turn 2 onward. So memory_recall_relevance/memory_recall_hit for the prompt of turn N land on Turn N-1's span, stamped metadata.attached_to:'turn' — downstream queries that trust that tag align scores to the wrong prompt. Only turn 1 behaves as the comment describes (no span yet -> root). Verify in Braintrust: for any session, the memory_recall_* score timestamps postdate the span they're attached to by one full turn. Fix: prefer root_span_id as the comment intends, or carry turn_count in the score metadata so consumers can realign.
telemetry: Braintrust: memory_recall_* scores with metadata.attached_to='turn' vs the turn span's own created timestamp — systematic one-turn lag
